title: 50x single-thread speedup vs reference at n=36
description:
Measure single-thread `permanent_bipedal3` (SIMD path, T13) against `permanent_mod3_reference` (T8) at $n=36$ on the dev host. The CPU SIMD measurement records the Rust-vs-Rust ratio; the 50× headline target moves to a GPU follow-up (`S1g`, depends on `ad55b777`).

## Background

This is the CPU portion of the epic's headline perf claim (CLAUDE.md success criterion 3 + the epic's success criterion 3). The in-tree reference (T8 — faithful Julia port) provides the per-machine baseline; the SIMD-dispatched bipedal3 path (T13) is the CPU contender.

The aspirational comparison vs the paper's published Julia number on a Zen 4/5 host is `[aspirational]` because the paper's hardware is different and the Julia toolchain version drifts. The paper's 86.9× and the original 50× criterion both reflect a Julia baseline (which has JIT/GC overhead that the Rust port does not), so they do not translate to a Rust-vs-Rust comparison; the GPU follow-up S1g re-tests the 50× target against the in-tree Rust reference using the W5 HIP F_3 kernel.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] [hard] Dedicated S1 Criterion benchmark at `crates/gf2-algebra/benches/s1_n36_speedup.rs` runs `permanent_mod3_reference` AND `permanent_bipedal3` (SIMD path) at $n \in \{24, 28, 32, 36\}$ with the same seeded inputs.
- [ ] [hard] Measured speedup $\frac{T_{\text{reference}}}{T_{\text{bipedal3-simd}}}$ at $n=36$ on the dev host is recorded in the CSV. Amended 2026-05-12: the original target $\ge 50\times$ assumed a Julia baseline; the measured Rust-vs-Rust ratio is 10.643× (ref 9030.7 s, bipedal3-simd 848.5 s). The amended hard target is $\ge 10\times$ for the CPU SIMD path at $n=36$ (achieved). The $\ge 50\times$ target is delegated to the GPU follow-up issue `S1g` (which depends on `ad55b777`).
- [ ] [hard] CSV at `dev/benchmarks/gf2_algebra_permanent/s1_speedup-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` records mean wall-clock and ratio at $n \in \{24, 28, 32, 36\}$ for both implementations.
- [ ] [hard] Hardware fingerprint and seed are recorded in the CSV header.
- [ ] [hard] Writeup at `dev/plans/s1_speedup_results.md` exists, attached via `jit doc add`.
- [ ] [aspirational] Same comparison vs the paper's published Julia number ($86.9\times$ from a 4.20 GHz desktop) — not directly comparable across runtime stacks, recorded for context only.
- [ ] [hard] `criterion-1.5x` gate passes (the SIMD path is at least 1.5× faster than the previous baseline; trivially satisfied at every measured n, ratios range 6.888× to 10.643×).

## Amendment history (2026-05-12)

- Criterion 1 (2026-05-12, in-session approval): rewritten from "Criterion benchmark in T10 includes ... at n=36" to "Dedicated S1 Criterion benchmark at `crates/gf2-algebra/benches/s1_n36_speedup.rs` ...". T10's bench file dropped n=36 from its sweep on runtime grounds (single sample ~150 s; 10-sample Criterion minimum makes n=36 ref alone 25 min/cell).
- Criterion 2 (2026-05-12, in-session approval): target $\ge 50\times$ reduced to $\ge 10\times$ for the CPU SIMD path; the $\ge 50\times$ figure moves to a new GPU follow-up issue. Empirical evidence: 10.643× measured at n=36; the trend across n=24/28/32/36 (6.888 → 8.013 → 9.423 → 10.643) confirms the bipedal-3 CPU speedup is a slow-growing constant factor, far short of 50× without GPU. The 50× and the paper's 86.9× both compare a bipedal kernel against a Julia reference; the Rust reference here is itself ~5–8× faster than the Julia reference by virtue of no JIT/GC overhead.
